question: does a fixed Gaussian prior on the embedding tables improve validation recall of the selected pooling and SASRec configurations?

penalty.objective_per_batch: (sum of batch sampled-softmax losses + embed_l2 * P_b) / k_b, with k_b targets in the batch
penalty.P_b: sum over the batch's input-row touches of |e_v|^2 / c_in(v) plus sum over output-row touches (positives and negative draws) of |w_v|^2 / c_out(v)
penalty.c_in: occurrences of the row in all training windows per epoch (deterministic)
penalty.c_out: positive occurrences per epoch + m T / N expected negative draws
penalty.epoch_total: about (1/mean k)(sum of all losses + embed_l2 (sum |input rows|^2 + sum |output rows|^2)): exact for input rows, in expectation for output rows
penalty.meaning: embed_l2 is the precision factor of a fixed Gaussian prior relative to the summed epoch loss; not comparable to AdamW weight decay, which is decoupled; SparseAdam has no weight decay
penalty.scope: both embedding tables, same embed_l2; transformer and LayerNorm parameters unpenalized; fixed-zero videos have no rows

control: embed_l2 = 0 = runs_20261020 (same code path; serial bitwise regression in implementation_checks.json)
budget: unchanged: max 20 epochs, tuning-half Recall@100 (filtered) every 2 epochs, stop after 3 evaluations without improvement, best checkpoint
logged: training loss (data term) and penalized objective each epoch; tuning-half Recall@100 and row-norm quantiles (p50, p90, p99, mean for degree <= 2 and >= 20) of both tables at each evaluation
screening: seed 42; select per encoder the level with the best tuning-half Recall@100 among {0, 1, 10, 100}
confirmation: only if the selected level is nonzero and beats embed_l2 = 0 on the tuning half by more than the step-23 report-half seed SD (pool 0.108 pp, SASRec 0.148 pp): seeds 1-4, compared with the five embed_l2 = 0 seeds on the report half (paired bootstrap, 2000, seed 2026)
reproducibility: runs execute two at a time; concurrent runs are not bitwise reproducible (float accumulation order), serial runs are
